newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary maize futures mixed, wheat down, barley up.
newsitem.headline: Hungary maize futures mixed, wheat down, barley up.

text.p: Maize futures prices ended mixed in the grain section of the Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE) with old crop prices finishing higher and new crop prices easing, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Old (1996) crop prices rose as some traders are not yet willing to deliver," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
Maize futures prices for December delivery closed at 19,800 forints, up 550, while March, May and July 1997 maturities rose by 90 to 250 forints.
"Opposite movements for the new (1997) crop were due to the fact that sellers were now willing to go lower," Monostori said.
Maize contracts for October 1997 closed at 21,000 forints, down 400, and for November 1997 at 21,450, down 350.
Milling wheat prices dropped for all maturities by 350 to 440 forints as most traders were seeking to close positions, Monostori said. @

Feed barley prices rose by 500 forints for December delivery to close at 27,800 forints, and also rose by 400 and 200 forints for July and August 1997, ending at 21,400 and 21,500 forints respectively, in very low turnover.
"There was no one on the selling side for weeks, so traders took the opportunity to buy while it was there," Monostori said.
Total turnover of the BCE grain section remained relatively low at 969 lots or 433 million forints, with maize and wheat contracts accounting for 885 lots.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts. @
